Levine Diabetes Care 2025;48(5):790–798 | https://doi.org/10.2337/dc24-2790 Conclusion: Tirzepatide-treated participants achieved clinically meaningful reductions in HbA1c and weight. Both early glucose and weight responses resulted in better longer-term metabolic outcomes. what_it_measured.text: However, the association between the early response to tirzepatide and longer-term outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes is not known.
What are late (week 40 or 42) metabolic outcomes, measured by early glycemic and weight response, in study participants with type 2 diabetes treated with tirzepatide?  What did we find?

dose.text: Tirzepatide was initiated at 2.5 mg once weekly for 4 weeks. Then, the dose was escalated in increments of 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until the randomized dose of 5, 10, or 15 mg was achieved.

endpoint.text: What are late (week 40 or 42) metabolic outcomes, measured by early glycemic and weight response, in study participants with type 2 diabetes treated with tirzepatide?  What did we find?

Composite End Point by Early Response Signiﬁcantly greater percentages of early versus nonearly responders (P # 0.01) achieved the composite end point of HbA1c <7% and $10% weight reduction at week 40 with all tirzepatide doses (Supplementary Fig. 1).

reported_results.text: Early responders in terms of glucose or weight achieved better metabolic outcomes at week 40 or 42.  What are the implications of our findings?

Composite End Point by Early Response Signiﬁcantly greater percentages of early versus nonearly responders (P # 0.01) achieved the composite end point of HbA1c <7% and $10% weight reduction at week 40 with all tirzepatide doses (Supplementary Fig. 1).

Comparison between early and nonearly responders was not statistically different with the tirzepatide 15-mg dose for the achievement of $10% weight reduction threshold in the analysis by early response in FSG.
Greater percentages of early versus nonearly responders achieved $10% and $15% weight reduction from baseline at week 40 with all tirzepatide doses in both analyses of early response (Fig. 2C–F).

Figure 3—Incidence of any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea events over time by early response in FSG [<20% (A) or $20% (B) reduction at week 4], or body weight [<5% (C) or $5% (D) reduction at week 8] in pooled tirzepatide-treated participants.

numbers.text: Tirzepatide was initiated at 2.5 mg once weekly for 4 weeks. Then, the dose was escalated in increments of 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until the randomized dose of 5, 10, or 15 mg was achieved.
What are late (week 40 or 42) metabolic outcomes, measured by early glycemic and weight response, in study participants with type 2 diabetes treated with tirzepatide?  What did we find?

Composite End Point by Early Response Signiﬁcantly greater percentages of early versus nonearly responders (P # 0.01) achieved the composite end point of HbA1c <7% and $10% weight reduction at week 40 with all tirzepatide doses (Supplementary Fig. 1).
Early responders in terms of glucose or weight achieved better metabolic outcomes at week 40 or 42.  What are the implications of our findings?

Comparison between early and nonearly responders was not statistically different with the tirzepatide 15-mg dose for the achievement of $10% weight reduction threshold in the analysis by early response in FSG.
Greater percentages of early versus nonearly responders achieved $10% and $15% weight reduction from baseline at week 40 with all tirzepatide doses in both analyses of early response (Fig. 2C–F).

Figure 3—Incidence of any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea events over time by early response in FSG [<20% (A) or $20% (B) reduction at week 4], or body weight [<5% (C) or $5% (D) reduction at week 8] in pooled tirzepatide-treated participants.
However, the association between the early response to tirzepatide and longer-term outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes is not known.
